name: BitPay
tagline: Longest-running major crypto payment processor: accept 100+ cryptocurrencies, settle in fiat daily, with no chargebacks.
shortDescription: Atlanta-based crypto payment processor operating since 2011. Merchants accept Bitcoin, Ethereum, stablecoins and 100+ other coins while BitPay locks the exchange rate at invoice time and settles fiat to the bank daily. Fees run 1% to 2% + 25 cents by volume.
longDescription:
BitPay was founded in 2011 in Atlanta and is the longest-operating major cryptocurrency payment processor, with rare regulatory footing for the niche: an NMLS money-transmitter registration and a New York BitLicense. Merchants accept more than 100 cryptocurrencies including Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Dogecoin and the major stablecoins, while customers pay from any wallet. The exchange rate locks when the invoice is created and BitPay converts instantly, so the merchant never holds crypto or takes volatility risk unless they choose crypto or stablecoin settlement.

Pricing and how it works

Fees are tiered by monthly paid-invoice volume: 2% + 25 cents below 500,000 dollars a month, 1.5% + 25 cents to 999,999 dollars, and 1% + 25 cents at a million dollars and above, with higher rates for high-risk industries. There is no monthly or setup fee, and because blockchain payments are push transactions there are no chargebacks at all. Buyers pay a separate network cost fee on top of the invoice. Settlement is calculated every business day, with fiat arriving in about one to two business days across eight currencies including USD, EUR and GBP, in 37 countries by bank transfer; crypto and stablecoin settlement reach 200+ countries. Refunds are possible but clunky: the merchant covers the network fee on a refund and the buyer's original network cost is not returned.

Who it is for

BitPay fits ecommerce, luxury goods, electronics, travel and precious metals sellers that want a no-chargeback payment rail for international customers, added alongside card processing rather than replacing it. Plugins cover Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento 2, BigCommerce, Wix and WHMCS, plus email billing and a retail app. Onboarding involves real KYB scrutiny, some verticals such as cannabis, weapons and MLM are prohibited, and demand is inherently niche: it is an additional payment option, not a primary processor.

data.html:
Accepting cryptocurrency directly can create a problem for merchants: customers may want to pay in crypto, but the business may not want to hold cryptocurrency itself.

BitPay is designed to help merchants accept supported cryptocurrency payments while providing settlement options that can reduce some of that complexity.

How BitPay Crypto Payments Work

The basic process is different from a normal card transaction.

A customer selects a supported cryptocurrency payment option, completes the payment, and the merchant receives settlement according to the BitPay account and payment configuration.

For businesses, the important question is what happens between the customer's crypto payment and the funds ultimately received by the merchant.

BitPay Pricing and Settlement Fees

When evaluating BitPay, consider the complete cost rather than only the processing percentage.

Look at:

  • Processing fees
  • Settlement fees
  • Currency conversion
  • Refund costs
  • Withdrawal or transfer costs
  • Supported settlement currencies

Who Is BitPay Best For?

BitPay is most relevant to businesses that have a genuine reason to accept cryptocurrency payments, such as:

  • Online businesses with crypto customers
  • Technology companies
  • International merchants
  • Businesses targeting crypto users
  • Merchants wanting crypto payment options without directly managing every part of the crypto transaction

Does BitPay Convert Crypto to Cash?

One of the key considerations for a merchant is whether cryptocurrency received from customers can be settled into a supported fiat currency rather than leaving the business exposed to crypto price movements.

Check the current settlement currencies and eligibility available to your business.

Is BitPay Safe?

Merchants should evaluate security controls, account protection, payment confirmation, refund procedures, settlement practices, and the risks associated with cryptocurrency payments before integrating any crypto payment provider.

faqs.question: How much does BitPay cost?
faqs.answer: Fees are tiered by monthly paid-invoice volume: 2% + 25 cents per transaction under 500,000 dollars a month, 1.5% + 25 cents between 500,000 and 999,999 dollars, and 1% + 25 cents at a million dollars and above. There are no monthly or setup fees and no chargeback fees. Buyers additionally pay a network cost fee that covers blockchain miner fees, and high-risk industries pay elevated rates.

faqs.question: How does BitPay protect merchants from crypto volatility?
faqs.answer: The exchange rate is locked the moment an invoice is created, and BitPay converts the payment instantly. Merchants receive the full fiat value regardless of what the coin does afterwards, with settlement calculated every business day and funds arriving in about one to two business days in USD, EUR, GBP or five other fiat currencies. Merchants who prefer can settle in 15 cryptocurrencies or stablecoins instead.

faqs.question: Can BitPay payments be charged back?
faqs.answer: No. Blockchain payments are push transactions and cannot be reversed by the buyer's bank, so the entire card chargeback mechanism does not exist. That makes BitPay attractive for high-ticket and international sales. Refunds remain possible, but they are merchant-initiated, and the blockchain network fee comes out of the refund.

faqs.question: Who should use BitPay?
faqs.answer: Ecommerce and high-ticket merchants such as luxury goods, electronics, travel and precious metals sellers that want a no-chargeback option for crypto-holding customers, especially internationally. It suits businesses adding crypto alongside card processing. Merchants in prohibited verticals such as cannabis, weapons, MLM and derivatives cannot use it, and every account goes through KYB verification.
